item.title: China says U.S. has no say on selection of BBNJ Secretariat seat
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese spokesperson said on Wednesday that the United States, which is neither a state party to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea nor to the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, has no say on the selection of the BBNJ Secretariat seat.
Guo Jiakun, the spokesperson for the Chinese foreign ministry, made the remarks when asked to comment on a statement issued by the U.S. State Department welcoming the joint bid by Chile and Belgium to host the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement.
"We call on all parties to stay vigilant against attempts to politicize the bidding and create confrontation in the process," said Guo.
He stressed that China has made clear its position on the Belgium-Chile proposal, adding that this joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects, namely, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement, procedural justice, established international practice, equitable geographical distribution, fair competition and the original commitment.
"According to the BBNJ Agreement, the seat of the Secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM), including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by the Conference of the Parties, and the CHM shall be managed by the Secretariat," said Guo.
These are the consensus as well as rights and responsibilities of all Parties to the Agreement, which no country has the right or is in any position to violate, he added.
"No one shall trade under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties, let alone coerce or hijack other Parties into accepting their proposal," Guo noted.
As one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China stands ready to work with the international community to uphold the original purpose of the Agreement and keep the selection of the Secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, so that the BBNJ Agreement can truly serve the shared interests of humanity, said Guo.

item.title: China urges Japan to accelerate destruction of abandoned chemical weapons
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
This photo taken on Nov. 25, 2026 shows the scene of a side event hosted by the Chinese delegation at the 31st Session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CSP-31) in The Hague, the Netherlands. China urged Japan to accelerate the destruction of abandoned chemical weapons in China at the CSP-31 in The Hague on Wednesday, stressing that prolonged delays in addressing the issue remain a major practical obstacle to achieving "a world free of chemical weapons." (Xinhua/Shao Haijun)
THE HAGUE, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China urged Japan to accelerate the destruction of abandoned chemical weapons in China at the 31st Session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CSP-31) in The Hague on Wednesday, stressing that prolonged delays in addressing the issue remain a major practical obstacle to achieving "a world free of chemical weapons."
The Chinese delegation hosted a side event titled "Current Status and Challenges with Respect to the Destruction of the Chemical Weapons Abandoned by Japan on the Territory of China," highlighting delays in the destruction process and calling on Japan to fulfill its obligations under the Convention. More than 100 representatives from over 40 countries attended the event.
According to the Chinese delegation, Japan has missed its deadlines for destroying the abandoned chemical weapons four times. The latest plan, adopted in 2022, is due to expire in 2027, putting Japan at risk of missing the deadline for a fifth time. Japan's budget for addressing the abandoned chemical weapons in China was cut by 22 percent this year compared with 2025, even as its defense budget continued to rise.
Shen Bo of China's Permanent Representation to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) said discussions at the Conference of the States Parties had reflected several shared understandings within the international community regarding the Japanese abandoned chemical weapons.
"Concerns are growing over delays in the destruction process, particularly the risk that Japan could miss the 2027 deadline. The international community expects Japan, as the state that abandoned the weapons, to fulfill its obligations under the Convention and accelerate their destruction," Shen said.
He said Japan must adopt a serious and responsible attitude toward its historical, political and legal responsibilities. Any attempt to whitewash its wartime crimes or rewrite history would not be accepted by China or the international community.
"Japan must show genuine commitment by faithfully fulfilling its obligations under the Convention and substantially increasing investment in personnel, technology and funding. It must also take swift action by providing accurate information on burial sites, improving the efficiency of excavation and recovery operations, and assuming responsibility for treating contaminated soil and water," Shen told Xinhua after the side event.
Vladimir Tarabrin of the Permanent Representation of the Russian Federation to the OPCW said Russia's position on the chemical weapons abandoned by Japan during World War II was "clear and unequivocal."
"This is not a matter of Japan's goodwill, nor is it an act of charity. It is Japan's legal and moral obligation to rid itself of this legacy of the Second World War as soon as possible," he added.
OPCW Director-General Sabrina Dallafior stressed that recovering and destroying the chemical weapons abandoned by Japan in China is an important part of the international community's shared goal of permanently and completely eliminating chemical weapons worldwide.
"This is a difficult task, but one that must be accomplished," she said.

item.title: China firmly opposes US's additional tariffs on China, other economies
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China's Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday that China firmly opposes the US Section 301 investigation under the pretext of "overcapacity," saying that the investigation is a typical unilateralist act that severely disrupts the international economic order and violates World Trade Organization rules.
Ministry spokesperson He Yadong made the remarks in reference to the US Trade Representative's recently announced findings of a Section 301 investigation into "overcapacity" and its proposed measures to impose additional tariffs on 14 economies, including China.
China urges the US to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation, He said, adding that China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.

item.title: Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries.
It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission.
In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station.
Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people.
Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago.
Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity.
For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people.
He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations.
Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship, opening Tiangong space station to first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
* China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani astronaut, into the orbiting Tiangong space station.
* The Shenzhou-24 mission, carried out by Chinese mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. Ali also became the first foreign astronaut to board Tiangong.
* China's manned space program has consistently adhered to the principle of peaceful utilization, equality and mutual benefit, and common development, while actively promoting international exchanges and cooperation and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind in outer space.
by Xinhua writers Li Minghao, Yi Ling and Quan Xiaoshu
JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani astronaut, into the orbiting Tiangong space station.
Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson for the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA), described the joint flight as a landmark achievement in bilateral cooperation as the two countries mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year, and an important manifestation of their traditional friendship.
China's manned space program has consistently adhered to the principle of peaceful utilization, equality and mutual benefit, and common development, while actively promoting international exchanges and cooperation and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind in outer space, Zhang said at a news conference on Tuesday.
UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said the United Nations welcomed the peaceful use of outer space and the international cooperation this mission represents.
Aboard a Long March-2F carrier rocket, the spaceship blasted off at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. About 10 minutes after liftoff, the spaceship separated from the rocket and entered its designated orbit. The CMSA declared the launch "a complete success."
The spacecraft completed a fast, automated rendezvous and docking with the front port of Tianhe, the station's core module, in about 3.5 hours. The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard Tiangong opened the hatch at 2:35 p.m. and welcomed the new arrivals.
The two crews then took group pictures marking the ninth space get-together in China's aerospace history.
After completing a short-term joint flight, Ali will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft alongside two Shenzhou-23 crew members. The other two Shenzhou-24 astronauts will stay in orbit for roughly six months along with Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu, who has already spent six months in orbit and will remain aboard Tiangong to complete a year-long stay experiment.
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua)
JOINT EXPERIMENTS
More than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests are planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission, covering space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine and new space technologies, according to the CMSA.
Four China-Pakistan cooperative projects in the fields of biotechnology and materials will be conducted during the Shenzhou-24 mission, and Ali will conduct an experiment on photosynthetic cyanobacteria, which was proposed by the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO).
The experiment is expected to provide a biological basis and data support for oxygen regeneration and biomanufacturing at future space stations and deep-space bases, said Chen Mengyun, who is in charge of international cooperation projects at the Technology and Engineering Center for Space Utilization under the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Another cooperative project, led by the University of Agriculture, Faisalabad in Pakistan, will expose 32 quinoa seed samples to the space environment outside the station for about one year to investigate their stress tolerance and longevity, with the aim of screening for superior varieties.
Describing Pakistan as one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change, Pakistani Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal said that the country needs smart and climate-resilient agriculture.
"The mission gives Pakistani scientists rare access to space laboratories, offering potential breakthroughs to boost productivity and climate resilience," he told Xinhua.
The other two experiments will focus on multilayer graphene-based hybrid composites and solar-heated self-healing carbon fiber composites, Chen said.
Pakistani Ambassador to China Syed Ali Asad Gillani said the four experiments in orbit will not only benefit Pakistani researchers, but also help advance the prosperity and development of all humanity.
China-Pakistan space cooperation spans more than three decades. In 1990, Pakistan's first experimental satellite, Badr-1, was launched aboard a Chinese rocket from the Xichang Satellite Launch Center. More recently, China launched Pakistan's cube satellite aboard the Chang'e-6 probe in 2024 and placed a Pakistani remote-sensing satellite in orbit via a Long March-6 rocket in April 2026.
This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali.(Xinhua)
COOPERATIVE TEAM
To support the joint flight, the Chinese side prepared bilingual Chinese-English manuals, provided food tailored to Ali's cultural and dietary habits, and tailored training and ceremonial attire for the Pakistani.
According to Shi Yusheng, an expert with the Astronaut Center of China, the center devised multiple methods to help Ali master Chinese commands and terminology critical for spaceflight. Beyond basic language courses, Ali received intensive training in high-frequency spaceflight vocabulary and commands. Later in the program, he was also taught classical Chinese poetry.
"With tight timelines and heavy tasks, we focused on spacecraft operations, pressure emergency response, fault handling and scientific experiments, and conducted high-frequency joint training to ensure the mission's success," Tang, the Shenzhou-24 mission commander, said at Tuesday's media briefing.
Wu, the mission flight engineer, said Ali had worked diligently to learn Chinese, while the Chinese crew used English as a supplementary communication tool. Through sustained effort, the crew progressed from merely understanding each other to anticipating each other's actions.
Ali can now communicate with his Chinese counterparts in Chinese. He described mastering flight skills, learning Chinese and forging close bonds with his Chinese crewmates as key gains from his training.
Ali said China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time. "Now it is time to show this great achievement in orbit and send the world a message that we work hand in hand for the peaceful utilization of space," he said.
In an interview with Xinhua, the Pakistani ambassador to China described the joint flight as taking bilateral relations "from Earth to space," calling it a dream come true for more than 250 million Pakistanis and "an excellent model for South-South cooperation."
This image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Nov. 25, 2026 shows a group picture of the crew of Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 spaceships. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
MULTIPLE TASKS
The Shenzhou-24 mission's main objectives are to complete an in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, maintain routine station operations, conduct space science and application work, and carry out maintenance, public outreach and payload tests.
One of the highlights is China's first year-long in-orbit stay experiment. The year-long test will establish a new system for studying the human body in space, conduct interdisciplinary frontier scientific experiments, explore and answer intrinsic mechanisms of human adaptation and remodeling in a spaceflight environment, build a space-human-body research database combining macro and micro perspectives, and produce a batch of original outcomes, said Zhang, the CMSA spokesperson.
In addition, the test will further accumulate practical experience in astronaut support technologies, enrich and improve the major safeguarding systems for in-orbit health, work and daily life, and steadily enhance the astronaut residency support capabilities of China's space station, he added.

item.title: Shenzhou-24 astronauts, including first foreigner, enter China's Tiangong space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
This image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Nov. 25, 2026 shows a group picture of the crew of Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 spaceships. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-24 crew, comprising Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, entered China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday.
Serving as a payload specialist, Ali has made history by becoming the first foreigner to board Tiangong.
The astronaut trio took off at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) the same day aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spaceship from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China.
The Shenzhou-23 crew in orbit opened the hatch of the space station at 2:35 p.m. and welcomed the new arrivals, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA).
After entering the space station, the Shenzhou-24 crew met with the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who have been in orbit for about six months. The two crews then took group pictures of the ninth space get-together in China's aerospace history. They will now start a new in-orbit handover round.
This image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Nov. 25, 2026 shows the crew of Shenzhou-24 entering China's Tiangong space station. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)
This image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Nov. 25, 2026 shows the crew of Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 spaceships talking with each other. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang)

item.title: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
This photo taken on July 4, 2025 shows the laptop production line of the carbon-neutral smart manufacturing factory of Lenovo in north China's Tianjin. (Xinhua/Zhao Zishuo)
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China has spearheaded the development of 78 international standards on artificial intelligence (AI), turning its industrial practices and technological innovations into global public goods, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR).
Sun Wei, deputy head of the department of standards innovation under the SAMR, told a press conference Tuesday that the body has made active efforts to help improve the international standards system architecture for AI.
Working with leading companies and top research institutions, the SAMR has led the development of 29 foundational and common international standards, covering key areas that include data governance, human-computer interaction, security and trustworthiness, Sun said.
In addition, the SAMR has coordinated the efforts of 15 technical standards bodies in developing 49 international standards for sector-specific applications, including smart cities and intelligent manufacturing, according to the official.
Sectoral application standards act as a key lever to drive the scaled and standardized implementation of AI technologies.
In recent years, the SAMR has expanded its efforts to advance international standards in key areas, such as smart manufacturing, smart cities, smart logistics and smart water management, drawing on China's extensive application scenarios and mature industrial practices.
Sun said China's systematic efforts to develop application-oriented standards across multiple industries offered technical standards and practical solutions for wider international adoption, supporting AI-empowered real economy development and inclusive, shared digital transformation.
The SAMR also revealed that, in response to common risks such as deepfakes and model "poisoning" in generative AI, China has jointly developed with multiple countries a guideline on addressing risks in generative AI.
According to the SAMR, this marked the world's first international standards proposal targeting generative AI governance and can provide key support for promoting the formation of a global consensus on risk management.

item.title: China's space station opens a new chapter in int'l cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. (Xinhua)
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-24 mission marks a milestone in China's manned space program as a Pakistani astronaut becomes the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station, opening a new chapter in China's efforts to advance international cooperation in space exploration.
Over the years, China has built its space station through independent innovation and technological development, demonstrating its growing capabilities in manned spaceflight. Its experience shows that self-reliance and international cooperation are not mutually exclusive. While independent development has laid a solid foundation for China's space program, openness is creating new opportunities for its continued progress.
China has increasingly sought to make its space program more accessible to international partners, offering opportunities for other countries to participate in scientific research and space exploration. The Shenzhou-24 mission is a concrete step in this direction.
For Pakistan, the mission offers an opportunity to develop expertise in human spaceflight, strengthen its astronaut training capabilities and participate in scientific experiments in orbit. For China, it marks the first joint spaceflight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts, extending bilateral cooperation into a new frontier. The experience could also pave the way for broader international participation in China's space program.
Space exploration transcends national borders and offers opportunities for countries to advance scientific knowledge through cooperation. China has consistently advocated the peaceful use of outer space and promoted international collaboration in this field.
A case in point is China's recent donation to the United Nations of a lunar soil sample collected by the Chang'e-6 mission from the far side of the Moon. By sharing the fruits of its space exploration with the international community, China is helping create opportunities for joint research and enabling more countries to benefit from advances in space science.
This photo taken on Sept. 14, 2026 shows a lunar sample collected from the far side of the Moon by China's Chang'e-6 mission, in Vienna, Austria. (Xinhua/He Canling)
Space exploration should not be an exclusive endeavor, but a shared undertaking that brings countries together through the exchange of knowledge, technology and talent. By opening its space station to international partners, China is creating opportunities for scientific collaboration and contributing to the peaceful use of outer space.
